name_en: Akutsu magari-negi — Koriyama's bent, replanted sweet leek
summary_ja: 郡山市阿久津地区で育てられる、根元から弓なりに曲がったねぎ。夏に一度掘り上げて斜めに植え直す「やとい」と呼ばれる手間をかけることで、白い部分が柔らかく甘くなるとされる。霜が降りてからの冬が旬という。
summary_en: A leek from the Akutsu district of Koriyama whose white stem bows in a deep curve. Dug up in midsummer and replanted at a slant in a step called yatoi, it is said to grow a softer, sweeter white stem, with its season arriving once frost has settled.

name_en: Aizu kogiku kabocha — a small, deeply ribbed heirloom pumpkin from Aizu
summary_ja: 会津地方で古くから自家採種で受け継がれてきた日本かぼちゃ。小菊の花のように深い縦溝が入った小ぶりの実で、ねっとりとした食感と控えめな甘みが煮物に向くとされる。会津伝統野菜のひとつに数えられる。
summary_en: A Japanese-type pumpkin kept going in the Aizu region by farmers saving their own seed. The small fruit is scored with deep vertical grooves like the petals of a small chrysanthemum, and its moist, dense flesh and restrained sweetness are said to suit simmered dishes. It is counted among the Aizu heirloom vegetables.
source_title: 会津若松市（公式サイト）

name_en: Kasumigaura renkon — lotus root from the marshy shores of Lake Kasumigaura
summary_ja: 霞ヶ浦の湖岸に広がる泥深い低地で育つれんこん。水を張った蓮田からポンプの水圧で泥を吹き飛ばして掘り上げる方法が広く行われ、白くて太い節とシャキシャキした歯ざわりが持ち味とされる。茨城県は国内のれんこん生産の大きな部分を占めるという。
summary_en: Lotus root grown in the deep mud of the lowlands rimming Lake Kasumigaura. Growers commonly harvest by blasting the mud away with a water jet in the flooded field, and the root is prized for its white, plump segments and crisp bite. Ibaraki is said to account for a large share of Japan's renkon.

name_en: Edosaki kabocha — vine-ripened, floury pumpkin from Inashiki
summary_ja: 稲敷市江戸崎周辺で育てられる西洋かぼちゃ。実が畑で完熟するまで待って収穫し、ほくほくとした粉質の果肉と強い甘みを引き出す作り方が特徴とされる。産地と作り方を結びつけて守る地理的表示（GI）に登録されている。
summary_en: A Western-type pumpkin grown around Edosaki in Inashiki. Growers wait until the fruit has fully ripened on the vine before picking, a practice said to give it floury, dense flesh and pronounced sweetness. The name is registered as a geographical indication tying the product to its place and method.
source_title: 地理的表示（GI）登録産品一覧

name_en: Tochigi yugao (fukube) — the bottle gourd peeled and sun-dried into kanpyo
summary_ja: 栃木県南部の下野市や壬生町一帯で栽培される大型の瓜。「ふくべ」とも呼ばれ、夏に穫れた実を帯状に薄く剥いて天日で干すとかんぴょうになる。国内のかんぴょうの大部分がこの地域で作られているとされる。
summary_en: A large gourd grown across Shimotsuke, Mibu, and the surrounding plain in southern Tochigi. Also called fukube, its summer fruit is peeled into long thin ribbons and sun-dried to become kanpyo (dried gourd strips). Most of the kanpyo made in Japan is said to come from this district.

name_en: Niisato negi — Utsunomiya's bent, replanted winter leek
summary_ja: 宇都宮市北部の新里町で受け継がれてきた曲がりねぎ。夏の終わりに一度掘り上げて斜めに植え直し、起き上がろうとする力で根元を曲げることで、白い部分が柔らかく甘くなるとされる。霜に当たった冬のものが旬という。
summary_en: A bent leek kept going in Niisato, in the hilly north of Utsunomiya. At the end of summer it is dug up and replanted at a slant, and the plant's effort to stand upright again bends the base, which is said to leave the white stem softer and sweeter. The season is winter, after frost.

name_en: Shimonita negi — thick, short winter leek that turns sweet in the pot, from Gunma
summary_ja: 群馬県下仁田町の限られた畑で育つ、太く短いねぎ。白い部分は直径が4〜5センチにもなり、生では辛みが強いが、火を通すととろりと崩れて強い甘みが出るとされる。霜に当たる晩秋から冬が旬で、すき焼きや鍋の具として知られる。
summary_en: A thick, short leek grown in a limited set of fields in Shimonita, Gunma. The white stem can reach four to five centimeters across; raw it is sharply pungent, but cooked it collapses into something soft and strongly sweet. Its season runs from late autumn into winter after frost, and it is known as a sukiyaki and hot-pot vegetable.

name_en: Fukaya negi — long white leek from the deep river soil of Saitama, sweetest in winter
summary_ja: 埼玉県深谷市を中心に作られるねぎ。利根川沿いの砂混じりの深い土で白い部分が長くまっすぐ伸び、繊維が柔らかく、霜に当たる冬は甘みが際立つとされる。特定の品種名ではなく、深谷で育てられたねぎの呼び名という。
summary_en: A leek grown around Fukaya in Saitama. In the deep, sandy soil along the Tone River the white stem grows long and straight, the fibers stay tender, and winter frost brings out a marked sweetness. The name is not a single variety but a term for leeks raised in the Fukaya district.

name_en: Koshigaya kuwai — blue-skinned arrowhead corm from Saitama's wet lowlands, simmered for New Year
summary_ja: 埼玉県東部の越谷市周辺の水田で育てられる、オモダカ科の水生野菜。青みがかった皮の丸い球茎から太い芽が伸び、「芽が出る」縁起物として正月の煮物に使われる。ほろ苦さとほくほくした食感が持ち味とされる。
summary_en: An aquatic vegetable of the arrowhead family, grown in flooded fields around Koshigaya in eastern Saitama. A thick shoot rises from the round, blue-tinged corm, and because 'the bud comes out' it is served at New Year as a good-luck food. A faint bitterness and a floury, chestnut-like texture are its hallmarks.

name_en: Yagiri negi — long white leek from the Edogawa riverbank at Matsudo, Chiba
summary_ja: 千葉県松戸市の江戸川沿い、矢切地区で育てられるねぎ。川が運んだ砂混じりの土で白い部分が長く伸び、繊維が柔らかく、霜に当たる冬は甘みが強いとされる。江戸へ野菜を運んだ近郊の畑の流れをくむという。
summary_en: A leek grown in the Yagiri district of Matsudo, Chiba, on the bank of the Edogawa river. In the sandy soil the river laid down, the white stem grows long, the fibers stay tender, and winter frost brings out a strong sweetness. It carries on the tradition of the market-garden fields that once fed Edo.
